correctness.rationale: Probability-sphere harmonic addition theorem gives the normalized quartic Gegenbauer kernel. Exactly two signed representatives per unordered support imply one antisymmetric block with eigenvalue 1-v and a symmetric Johnson two-subset block. Unsigned incidence BB*= (d-2)I+11* identifies all three Johnson sectors and their dimensions. Substitution u=P(1/2), v=P(0) factors the four exact rational eigenvalues. Their zeros identify only d=8 in the theorem domain. Algebraic derivatives prove the positive squared singular values are >=11/640 at every integer d>=5, with equality in the d=9 standard sector. The standalone checker reconstructs the full rational Gram and tests all eigenspace generators for d=3..12, and checks closed forms through d=500; all were reproduced. These finite checks are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The novel mathematical assertion is the joint all-d>=5 degree-four signed-root spectral and interpolation classification, particularly the seven-dimensional d=8 exception and sharp dimension-uniform least-positive eigenvalue 11/640 at d=9. The earlier harmonic-design sources give an addition theorem and particular spherical design vanishing, not the stated complete spectrum or cross-dimension optimal stability. Classical Johnson eigenvalues are credited as input. Priority remains qualified because a broader root-scheme eigenmatrix or its optimized specialization might already cover the result.

value.rationale: For canonical D_d root samples, this is a complete natural infinite-dimensional family of exact-degree-four interpolation problems. The rank is full in every d>=5 except d=8, where exactly seven independent sample constraints have explicit vertex-incidence description; hence the result determines feasible data. The sharp all-dimensional positive spectral bound 11/640 and extremizing d=9 give an optimal dimension-independent L2 interpolation norm rather than a generic full-rank statement. These are structurally motivated quantitative invariants with direct reconstruction use, not an arbitrary finite slice.
